title: G6 On new sensor start, data with timestamp before new sensor was started is sent to NS and AAPS
body:
### Subject of the issue
When new G6 sensor is started, old data (data accumulated before new sensor was started) is being added to NS and send over broadcast. This seems like similar issue to https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/1778 and solution might be the same. Once new sensor is started, all data from before should be ignored and dropped. Is this something that could be easily implemented? 

### Expected behavior
Data before sensor start is dropped.

### Actual behavior
When sensor starts all data is sent to NS and broadcast.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Start new G6 sensor and look at data

### Additional notes
So new version of AAPS (3.0 - current betas), stops Loop as soon is it receives such data (new BgQualityPlugin). This is why all AAPS users are being warned not to use Xdrip anymore. If this could be fixed sooner, rather the later, warning about Xdrip probably won't go in release...

comments.body: I did ask on Gitter, but there was no response... It is true I didn't have all the details yet at that point, but this is valid issue, that will soon affect a lot of users of Xdrip (everybody that is using AndroidAPS that is).
https://github.com/Navid200/xDrip/discussions/148 discusson for additional info on the topic

After looking at some of the source code, my guess is that xDrip decides to request a backfill (as the last bg values are quite old) on the first bg value from a new sensor, see https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/blob/master/app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/G5Model/Ob1G5StateMachine.java#L803 - will have to start a new sensor anyway in a couple of days; will see if I get around to having logcat open then at the 2h mark.
Maybe this backfill then requests some stale data from the transmitter and ends up with old data from the old sensor?

I can confirm that after a sensor change and warmup (2h) AAPS receives (a backfill) 3h of BG data. 

Why is a backfill requested in Xdrip?
Is the problem that AAPS wont accept out of order data or that it wont accept data before the sensor start time?

The code in question sits in https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/blob/dev/app/src/main/java/info/nightscout/androidaps/plugins/constraints/bgQualityCheck/BgQualityCheckPlugin.kt#L79 - so it receives bg values from xDrip that are less than 20ms apart; so duplicate values with different timestamps.
So the issue seems to be that xDrip is broadcasting values that were already broadcasted before - but with a slightly different timestamp.
Isn't that 20 seconds expressed in ms? rather than 20ms difference?

I'm pretty sure that xDrip is doing de-duplication of readings based on timestamp before it processes them. This should apply to upload to nightscout and local broadcast. There could be a bug with this code or something else could be happening. It would be very interesting if a user who has experienced this problem with AAPS could provide what the reading timestamps look like from that red warning code that @savek-cc linked - for example are they identical timestamps or slightly different?

@jamorham I think problem is that they are "slightly" different, but still within that 20s range. If they were the same NS and AAPS  would detect that, but they seem to be just little "off", so they get treated as new record.

@MilosKozak i thought that code was supposed to check for duplicates within a couple of ms - but apparently it really is 20 seconds that are checked here? Could you *please* provide a short explainaition from your understanding of the issue and what these 20 seconds are about (as I can't really understand what is cought there in the bg quality plugin)?
@jamorham it used to be less: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/22eb5245562567e3264cbb09580f16b7b1ce3517
@andyrozman Is this problem for data which is being delivered from xDrip via local broadcast or after being uploaded to nightscout (or both) ?

I would imagine both. 
If you send it via broadcast there will be a problem and if it comes from NS also. AAPS look at all data it receives and checks for duplicates within those 20s...

I'm not sure about NS and i don't know if xdrip even sends bg updates from the past to the NS.
 But it's definitely broadcasted to AAPS
@MilosKozak as I can't understand that check function: can you explain in plain English what that function checks for with the 20 seconds?

SQL on this one:
`SELECT * from (
SELECT _id, calculated_value, timestamp, source_info,
(timestamp - LAG (timestamp, 1) OVER (ORDER BY timestamp)) as diff_ms,
strftime('%d-%m-%Y %H:%M:%S', datetime(timestamp/1000, 'unixepoch')) time_str,

@savek-cc thanks for your analysis. Where you have close timestamps do these have a different sensor id column? I'm suspecting they do as the xDrip de-duplication is filtered by sensor session which maybe it also shouldn't be but it is possible for different sensor session id's to have duplicated backfilled data which I expect is likely part of the reason for this issue. What I have done is capped the backfill window start to the current sensor session start which I'm thinking will have a similar effect.

@MilosKozak so https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/commit/6f7c3660d6e140d914f24a155a0bcffa810ab4d8 should fix the issue towards both NS and AAPS.
For reference: If you want to analyze and xDrip-Backup for this event, you can use the following SQL to get all pairs that are within 20 seconds of each other:
`SELECT * from (
SELECT _id, sensor, sensor_uuid, calculated_value, timestamp, source_info,
abs (timestamp - LAG (timestamp, 1) OVER (ORDER BY timestamp)) as diff_ms1,
abs (timestamp - LAG (timestamp, -1) OVER (ORDER BY timestamp)) as diff_ms2,
strftime('%d-%m-%Y %H:%M:%S', datetime(timestamp/1000, 'unixepoch')) time_str,
time_since_sensor_started / (1000*60) as sensor_age_min
FROM BgReadings WHERE source_info NOT NULL ORDER BY timestamp) where (diff_ms1 < 20000 or diff_ms2 < 20000);`
